notes.decision: Preserved untranslated as decorative section/title-frame marker. The pattern 'leer ⲧ̄ⲧ ... ⲧ̄ⲧ' frames the chapter heading on lines 3-5, paralleling the page-header decoration '> · ⲛⲕⲉⲫⲁⲗⲁⲓⲟⲛ · <'. The repeated marker likely functions as ornamental divider rather than as lexical content. May represent an abbreviated marker or sigil whose exact reference is not recoverable.

Read as 'The Chapter of the Commandments of Righteousness.' The word ⲉⲛⲧⲟⲗⲁⲩⲉ (Greek ἐντολαί + Lyc. plural -ⲁⲩⲉ) is split across the line break with the ⲧ̄ⲧ marker intervening — ⲛⲉⲛⲧⲟ | ⲧ̄ⲧ ⲗⲁⲩⲉ. ⲛⲧⲁⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥⲩⲛⲏ is regular Lyc. for ⲛ̄ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥⲩⲛⲏ. The chapter that follows enumerates the three seals (sexual continence, manual rest, oral purity) plus the second righteousness of giving wisdom/faith/grace/love — these are the 'commandments of righteousness.'

notes.coptic_form: ⲧⲉⲣⲕⲣⲁⲧⲉⲓⲁ ⲙⲛ ⲡⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ ⲛ̄ⲭⲭⲡⲟ ... ⲡⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ ⲛ̄ⲛⲟ̄ⲓⲭ ... ⲡⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ ⲛⲧⲧⲁⲡⲣⲟ
notes.decision: These three items are the canonical Manichaean Three Seals (signacula): (1) continence + purity of begetting = signaculum sinus (sexual seal); (2) the rest of the hands = signaculum manuum (manual seal, abstaining from harming the Living Soul through manual labor on plants/the cross of light); (3) the purity of the mouth = signaculum oris (oral seal, abstention from flesh/blood/wine). The text explicitly numbers the third as ⲡⲙⲁϩⲱⲁⲙⲧ 'the third' (line 11), confirming the enumeration.

Translated 'For him also' (= ⲛⲁϥ ⲁⲛ in Sahidic), where ⲭ = 3sg.m suffix in Lycopolitan (cf. ⲡⲉⲭ-/ⲡⲉϩ- 'his' in glossary). Functions as transitional discourse marker introducing the second seal. Could alternatively be a fixed connective 'moreover,' but the dative reading is consistent with ⲛⲉⲭ in line 22 where 'beget for him' is unambiguous.

Translated 'the name (called) wine.' The Manichaean elect abstained absolutely from wine; the phrase 'not to take a taste of the name wine' emphasizes the totality of the prohibition — even the substance bearing the name. Cf. parallel commandments forbidding 'flesh and blood.'
Translated 'and at any time.' Greek καιρόν 'time, season' with the conjunction ϩⲓ; ⲥⲓ- may be an indefinite/adverbial particle ('any') or a Lyc. orthographic feature.

Translated 'the second righteousness, however.' The structure of the chapter has 'first righteousness = bodily seals' (lines 7-15) and 'second righteousness = giving wisdom/faith/grace/love to others' (lines 16-25). The second is the dispensational/teaching righteousness of the perfected Elect.
Translated 'give himself.' Idiom ϯ ⲁϫⲱ⸗ 'devote oneself to' — the perfected Elect gives himself over wholly to wisdom and faith.

Translated 'while other ones he sets among them.' The Elect serves as a model in whose likeness others (catechumens) are arranged within the community of righteousness. ⲭⲁⲧⲉ functions as a temporal/circumstantial conjunction.

Translated 'being completed in two manners.' The catechumenate has two perfections (= the fast/prayer/mercy triad on the one hand, and other works on the other). The text immediately enumerates the first as fast+prayer+mercy.
